beats.beat: The core of the business is processing minerals and chemicals. The filing lists four product lines: functional additives (FA), chemically modified minerals (CMM), soft minerals (SM) and hard minerals (HM).
The company cites a diversified product portfolio and diversified user industries among its strengths.
It also claims import substitution as a strength, aligning with India's larger chemical trade deficit.
Its route to market runs through the promoter's network; the company says it derives 'substantial synergies' from 20 Microns Limited.
Customer concentration is high: top 10 customers generated around 59% of revenue from operations in FY2015, FY2016 and FY2017.
Over the past five years it exported ₹10.68 crore worth of goods (₹1068.18 lakh), with Nigeria, Saudi Arabia and Sri Lanka named.
The company also lists product innovation and continuous R&D as a competitive strength.

beats.beat: The restated summary financial statements cover six periods: the six months ended September 30, 2017, and full years FY2017, FY2016, FY2015, FY2014 and FY2013.

Profit after tax: ₹1.33 crore in H1 FY18 and ₹1.75 crore in FY2017, up from ₹0.90 crore in FY2016 and ₹1.50 crore in FY2015. The company recorded small losses of ₹0.12 crore in FY2014 and ₹0.27 crore in FY2013.
Basic EPS: ₹1.48 in H1 FY18, ₹2.43 in FY2017, ₹1.46 in FY2016, ₹2.47 in FY2015, and negative ₹0.20 and ₹0.45 in FY2014 and FY2013.

Cash flow from operations: ₹1.25 crore inflow in H1 FY18, but a ₹3.50 crore outflow in FY2017, after inflows of ₹8.03 crore in FY2016, ₹4.22 crore in FY2015, ₹1.28 crore in FY2014 and ₹2.01 crore in FY2013.
Total assets stood at ₹34.25 crore at September 30, 2017, compared with ₹30.19 crore at March 31, 2013; assets dipped to ₹25.93 crore at FY2015 before climbing back.
The filing also discloses contingent liabilities aggregating ₹29.11 lakh as of September 30, 2017.
Revenue, EBITDA and debt figures are not in the available excerpts; the profitability trend should be read alongside the cash flow, which turned negative in FY2017 despite a reported profit.

beats.beat: The promoters are 20 Microns Limited (the corporate promoter) and three individuals: Chandresh S. Parikh, Atil C. Parikh and Rajesh C. Parikh.
Pre-issue, the promoters hold 99.76% of the paid-up equity capital (89,48,270 shares); the promoter group holds the remaining 0.24% (21,510 shares).
Authorised share capital is ₹20 crore (2 crore equity shares of ₹10 each); issued, subscribed and paid-up capital is ₹8.97 crore (89.7 lakh shares).
The company has had related-party transactions with promoter-group entities in each of the last five years and the six months to September 30, 2017.

The filing discloses past instances of non-filing or delayed filings with the Registrar of Companies, and says certain statutory approvals for a manufacturing facility at Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia, are yet to be obtained.
Outstanding legal proceedings involve the company, its promoters, group companies and directors, any adverse outcome of which could hurt the business.

beats.beat: The specialty chemicals segment of India's chemicals industry was worth about ₹1,000 billion in fiscal 2017, roughly 17% of the total chemicals pie.
Specialty chemicals grew at 10-12% CAGR from fiscal 2014 to fiscal 2017, and CRISIL Research projects 12-14% CAGR looking ahead.

Within that, the filing highlights faster-growing downstream segments: construction chemicals, water chemicals and personal care ingredients are each expected to expand at 15% CAGR, with polymer additives at 10%.
The industry is highly fragmented — SMEs hold 70-75% of the market — and only a few Indian players can match global giants on product development and innovation.
India runs a chemical trade deficit: imports grew at 6.4% CAGR versus 6% for exports between fiscal 2013 and fiscal 2017.

Demand drivers the filing cites include rising consumption, urbanisation — urban population was 31% in 2011 and is expected to reach 36% by 2020 — and government initiatives including a draft National Chemical Policy and 100% FDI allowance.
Headwinds acknowledged in the filing include REACH regulation for exports to Europe, GST implementation from July 1 2017, and competition from global players.

beats.beat: 20 Microns Nano Minerals Limited is a Vadodara-based company that processes and sells specialty chemicals — functional additives, chemically modified minerals, and soft and hard minerals.
Its business model is unusual: it sells through the marketing network of its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited, under a long-term arrangement.
The company wants to raise money in an SME IPO to fund a new manufacturing facility at GIDC Waghodia and for general corporate purposes, and to get its shares listed on NSE EMERGE.
The issue is being managed by Vivro Financial Services Private Limited, with Link Intime India Private Limited as registrar.

intro.purpose: Orient the reader: who this company is, what it does, what it is raising and why it matters.

beats.beat: The stated objects of the issue are: to fund capital expenditure on a new manufacturing facility at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara; general corporate purposes; and to create a public trading market for the shares by listing on NSE EMERGE.
The lead manager is Vivro Financial Services Private Limited and the registrar is Link Intime India Private Limited.
The available excerpts do not disclose the issue size, price band, or whether there is an offer-for-sale component; this report flags that gap rather than guessing.

beats.beat: Customer concentration without contracts: around 59% of revenue comes from the top 10 customers, and sales are on purchase orders, not long-term agreements — so a large customer can walk away or squeeze prices.

Negative operating cash flow: FY2017 produced a ₹3.50 crore outflow from operations despite a profit, and the company itself warns that negative cash flows in previous financial years could impact growth.
It does not own the premises for two manufacturing facilities (Plot 347, GIDC Waghodia, and Plot 104/3, Thenkasi Road, Tirunelveli) or its administrative offices in Bhuj and Udaipur.
The company admits it has not yet obtained all statutory and regulatory approvals for the manufacturing facility at Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia, and could be penalised for non-compliance.
Related-party dependence: the business depends on its corporate promoter's marketing network, and the company has a history of related-party transactions, creating the risk of conflicts of interest.
